title: Faith, hope and charity (CCC 1812–1829)
hook: three virtues given by God, and the greatest is charity

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Beatitudes: eight blessings that sound backwards and paint a portrait of Jesus. Your line was blessed are. Today, three words often heard at weddings.

If you've been to a wedding, you've probably heard it. Someone's cousin walks up to the lectern, a little nervous, and reads: charity is patient, is kind. Or, in other Bibles, love is patient, love is kind. Everyone nods. It sounds written for the couple. It wasn't. Paul wrote it to a church in Corinth that was fighting: over leaders, over gifts, over who was more spiritual. And he ended with three words, and a ranking. The Church has built a whole teaching on those three, and calls them different from every other virtue.
screen: `A COUSIN AT THE LECTERN.` → `WRITTEN TO A CHURCH IN A FIGHT.` → `THREE WORDS, AND A RANKING.`

segments.voice: The verse, in the Douay-Rheims: "And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity." Why theological? Theos is Greek for God. The Catechism calls these the theological virtues because they come from God, are aimed at God, and are about God directly. Other virtues, like patience or courage, can be built by practice. These three, Catholics say, are given: poured in by God, first at baptism. A person can grow in them, but doesn't invent them. Faith is believing God and all he has revealed. Hope is desiring God's kingdom and eternal life, and trusting his promises, relying not on your own strength but on grace. Hebrews calls hope "an anchor of the soul, sure and firm." Not optimism, which depends on how things look: hope holds even when things look bad. And charity is loving God above all things, and your neighbor as yourself, for God's sake. Why is charity greatest? In the Latin Bible it's caritas, in the Greek agape: not a feeling, not a donation, but a love that wills the good of the other. Paul describes it: "Charity is patient, is kind: charity envieth not, dealeth not perversely; is not puffed up." And why it's greatest: "Charity never falleth away." Now, he says, we see through a glass in a dark manner, but then face to face. Catholics read this to mean that one day faith will become sight, hope will be fulfilled, and charity will remain.
screen: `FAITH, HOPE, CHARITY: THESE THREE.` · `FROM GOD, AIMED AT GOD.` · `HOPE: AN ANCHOR, NOT OPTIMISM.` · `CHARITY NEVER ENDS.` · then, large: `THE GREATEST OF THESE IS CHARITY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing that feels stuck: a worry, a relationship, a situation that isn't changing. Don't pretend it's fine, because hope isn't pretending; just picture dropping an anchor beside it, something that holds even while the water moves. If you pray, you can hand it to God and let him hold the rope; if you don't, just hold the anchor.
Theological virtues. Faith, hope and charity: three virtues Catholics say are given by God and aimed at God, and the greatest of them is charity.
Your line: the greatest is charity. Patient, kind, and never falling away. That's day three hundred thirteen.

howItsDone: Some Catholics pray short traditional acts of faith, hope and charity, and 1 Corinthians 13 is one of the readings a couple may choose for a Catholic wedding.
